name: Neal Brennan
note: STAGE PERSONA graph for the 'Why is X Funny?' video series. Graph-only. Hypothesis unless sets measured. Stage persona only.

identity.deal: Co-creator brain doing solo autopsy: treats his own depression, success, and Chappelle-adjacent history as material for the most honest hour on the circuit.
identity.premise: A man who helped invent modern comedy's biggest voice, then turned the lens on himself with uncomfortable precision.
identity.awareness_note: Brutally aware; the honesty is the act and the wound.

philosophy.ontology: Success doesn't fix the brain; it gives the brain better material.
philosophy.epistemology: If it hurts to say, it's probably the bit.
philosophy.axiology: Honesty over comfort, even when the honesty is about yourself.
philosophy.causality: One uncomfortable truth told well frees the room.
philosophy.agency: Anyone can confess; almost nobody autopsies.

dramatic_core.want: to say the true thing even when it costs
dramatic_core.fear: the comfortable lie — his own most of all
dramatic_core.need: the room to sit in the discomfort with him
dramatic_core.self_model: a man doing surgery on himself in public
blind_spots: the honesty can become a performance of honesty

identity.misinterpretation_rule: Treats his own life as a case study, applies the same rigor he'd apply to someone else's, reports the findings without flinching.
contradictions: the architect dissecting his own building
the funny one doing the sad hour

tells: the laugh that covers the crack

threads: honesty as a weapon and a wound

internal.cite: Attardo & Raskin — General Theory of Verbal Humor
internal.claim: Joke = {SO, LM, SI, TA, NS, LA}. Technique and Narrative Strategy shape how the mechanism is staged.

internal.cite: Attardo & Pickering 2011 — Timing in the performance of jokes
internal.claim: Punch lines preceded by substantial pauses (0.6-0.8s+); timing = pause distribution + speech rate.

internal.cite: arxiv 2605.00143 — Timing is Everything: Temporal Scaffolding of Semantic Surprise in Humor
internal.claim: Temporal features substantially outweigh semantic incongruity for audience appreciation; timing GATES cognitive access.
Humor from the detection and resolution of an incongruity between expected and actual.
Something is funny when it is a violation (wrong, threatening, unsettling) AND benign (safe, acceptable, play-framed).

internal.cite: Roger & Duffy / status theory of humor
internal.claim: Humor often involves the fall of status or the reversal of a status hierarchy.
Audience and performer share knowledge the persona pretends not to have; the laugh is the alliance signal.

internal.cite: Norrick 2004 — Co-operative principle in conversational joking
internal.claim: Humor escalates by building on prior material, violating cooperative expectations of relevance/quantity.
